test: Michigan Driver's License Knowledge Test (operator, Class O)
edition: Based on 'What Every Driver Must Know' (Michigan Department of State, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025; PDF dated January 2026 on michigan.gov/sos), plus Michigan State Police OHSP 'Impaired Driving Law' page for BAC limits. Checked October 2026.

exam.rules: Adults (18 and older) who have never been licensed take the written knowledge test, which includes a separate road-sign portion, before a Temporary Instruction Permit (TIP) is issued. It is multiple choice, offered free at a computer station in a Secretary of State office (arrive at least one hour before closing) or online at home for a $6.50 fee; both portions (an 'Operator' section of about 45 minutes and a 'Signs' section of about 15 minutes) must be passed. Failing ends that day's session and you must retest on another day; passed results are valid for one year. Teens under 18 do not take the SOS test: they pass the Segment 1 state exam (minimum 70 percent) in a certified driver education course before getting a Level 1 Learner's License. Michigan does not publish the exact number of questions; this mock uses the commonly reported 50 questions (25 operator + 25 signs) with 80 percent needed on each part.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to enroll in Segment 1 driver education in Michigan?
questions.explain: Teens must be at least 14 years and 8 months old, with parental permission, to begin Segment 1.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: What is the minimum age for a GDL Level 1 Learner's License?
questions.explain: A Level 1 Learner's License can be issued at 14 years, 9 months after Segment 1 is completed.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: What minimum score must a teen earn on the Segment 1 and Segment 2 state exams?
questions.explain: Both driver education segments require at least 70 percent on the state exam.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: With a Level 1 Learner's License, who may supervise the teen driver?
options: Any licensed driver age 18 or older riding anywhere in the vehicle
A licensed parent, guardian, or a designated licensed adult age 21 or older seated in the front seat
questions.explain: Level 1 drivers may drive only with a licensed parent, guardian or designated licensed adult 21+ in the front seat beside them.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a Level 1 driver log before taking the driving skills test?
questions.explain: A minimum of 50 logged hours, 10 of them at night, is required before the skills test.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: Before starting Segment 2, a teen must have logged at least how many hours of supervised driving?
options: 30 hours, including at least 2 hours at night
questions.explain: Segment 2 requires a log of at least 30 supervised hours (2 at night) and a Level 1 license held at least 3 consecutive months.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: How long must a teen have held a Level 1 Learner's License before enrolling in Segment 2?
questions.explain: Segment 2 requires the Level 1 license to have been held for at least three consecutive months.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a GDL Level 2 Intermediate License?
questions.explain: A Level 2 license requires age 16, six months on Level 1, and a clean record for the preceding 90 days.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: To advance to Level 2, a teen's driving record must be free of violations, at-fault crashes and suspensions for how long before applying?
questions.explain: There must be no violations, at-fault crashes or suspensions in the 90 days before the Level 2 application.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: A Level 2 Intermediate License holder may not drive during which hours unless an exception applies?
questions.explain: Level 2 drivers may not drive between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. unless supervised by a qualifying adult or driving for work or an authorized activity.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: Under a Level 2 license, how many passengers under age 21 may ride with the teen (when no exception applies)?
questions.explain: Level 2 drivers may carry no more than one passenger under 21 unless a qualifying adult is present, the passengers are immediate family, or it is work or an authorized activity.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: Which situation is an exception to the Level 2 passenger restriction?
options: The passengers are members of the teen's immediate family
The passengers are all age 18 or older
It is daytime on a weekend
The trip is shorter than 10 miles
questions.explain: Immediate family passengers are exempt, as are trips with a qualifying adult or for work or authorized activities; age 18-20 passengers still count.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: What is required to receive a GDL Level 3 Full License?
options: Be at least 16 and pass a second driving skills test
Be at least 17, hold Level 2 for 6 months, and drive 12 consecutive months without a moving violation, at-fault crash, suspension or GDL violation
Be at least 18 and pay a full license fee
questions.explain: Level 3 requires age 17, six months on Level 2 and 12 consecutive clean months; it is issued automatically at no fee.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: At what age does Michigan's Graduated Driver Licensing program end?
questions.explain: GDL ends when the driver turns 18.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Under 18 – Graduated Driver Licensing'

questions.q: What does Kelsey's Law prohibit?
options: Passengers under 16 from riding in the front seat
Level 1 and Level 2 GDL drivers using a cell phone while driving, except in an emergency
All drivers from eating while driving
questions.explain: Kelsey's Law bars GDL Level 1 and Level 2 drivers from phone use while driving except to report an emergency.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Cell phone use prohibited for all drivers – including teens'

questions.q: How long is a Michigan temporary instruction permit (TIP) valid?
questions.explain: A TIP is valid for 180 days.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Temporary instruction permit'

questions.q: An adult on a TIP must practice for at least how long before taking the driving skills test?
questions.explain: Adults must complete at least 30 days of supervised practice on a TIP before the skills test.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Temporary instruction permit'

questions.q: Which tests must an adult pass before a temporary instruction permit is issued?
options: A written test only; vision is tested later
A vision test plus the written knowledge and road sign tests
questions.explain: To get a TIP you must pass the vision test and the written knowledge and road sign tests and meet health standards.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Temporary instruction permit'

questions.q: Once passed, how long are Michigan knowledge test results valid?
questions.explain: Passed knowledge test results are valid for one year (a new test is needed if a TIP is reapplied for after expiring).
questions.ref: Michigan SOS web page 'New drivers (18 and older)' (michigan.gov/sos)

questions.q: If you must take a knowledge test at a Secretary of State office, when should you arrive?
options: At least one hour before closing
Only first thing in the morning
questions.explain: Arrive at least one hour before closing to allow time to complete the test.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Vision and knowledge tests'

questions.q: New Michigan drivers, including GDL teens, are placed on probation for a minimum of:
questions.explain: All newly licensed drivers are on probation for at least three years.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Probationary license program'

questions.q: How long is a Michigan driver's license usually valid?
options: Four years, expiring on your birthday
questions.explain: Licenses are usually valid four years and expire on your birthday (under-21 licenses expire on the 21st birthday).
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Renewing your license'

questions.q: If you are under age 21, when does your Michigan driver's license expire?
options: Four years after issue regardless of age
questions.explain: A driver's license held by someone under 21 expires on the 21st birthday.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Renewing your license'

questions.q: What can happen if you move and fail to change your address with the Secretary of State?
options: Your license may be suspended or revoked
Your vehicle registration is cancelled immediately
questions.explain: Michigan requires your license address to match your residence; failure to change it can lead to suspension or revocation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Changing information on your license'

questions.q: A person who has never been licensed anywhere will be refused a Michigan license if they have:
options: One moving violation in the past five years
Any parking ticket in the past year
Two or more moving-violation convictions within three years of applying
questions.explain: An applicant never previously licensed may have no more than one conviction on record within three years of the application.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Licensing requirements'

questions.q: A new resident with a valid license from which of these places can convert it without the written, TIP and skills tests?
questions.explain: Licenses from other U.S. states, Canada, Germany and South Korea can be converted without those tests.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 1, 'Moved to Michigan from another state or country'

questions.q: For a driver age 21 or older, what bodily alcohol content (BAC) makes driving a crime in Michigan?
questions.explain: It is a crime for a driver 21 or older to drive with a BAC of .08 or more; drivers can be arrested at lower levels if impaired.
questions.ref: Michigan State Police OHSP, 'Impaired Driving Law' (michigan.gov/msp)

questions.q: For a driver under age 21, Michigan's zero-tolerance law applies at what BAC?
questions.explain: Michigan's zero-tolerance law for drivers under 21 covers a BAC of .02 or more, and also any presence of alcohol from drinking (the handbook gives 4 points for any bodily alcohol content).
questions.ref: Michigan State Police OHSP, 'Impaired Driving Law' (michigan.gov/msp)

questions.q: Michigan's high-BAC ('super drunk') law applies to drivers with a BAC of:
questions.explain: Enhanced penalties apply at a BAC of .17 or higher.
questions.ref: Michigan State Police OHSP, 'Impaired Driving Law' (michigan.gov/msp)

questions.q: What is the BAC limit for a person driving a commercial motor vehicle in Michigan?
questions.explain: Commercial drivers may not operate with a BAC of .04 or more (MCL 257.625m).
questions.ref: Michigan Vehicle Code MCL 257.625m; Michigan Commercial Driver License Manual

questions.q: How many points are added to your record for operating while intoxicated?
questions.explain: Operating while intoxicated (or with any Schedule 1 drug or cocaine) is a six-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: A driver under 21 convicted of driving with any bodily alcohol content receives how many points?
questions.explain: Under 21 with any bodily alcohol content is a four-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: How many points does refusing a chemical (alcohol) test carry?
questions.explain: Refusal to take a chemical alcohol test is a six-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: Refusing a Preliminary Breath Test (PBT) is a 2-point violation for which drivers?
questions.explain: Refusal of a PBT by anyone younger than 21 carries two points.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: Under Michigan's implied consent law, when are drivers considered to have agreed to chemical testing?
options: Only when they sign a form at the scene
Only if they have a prior conviction
When they apply for or renew their driver's license
questions.explain: All drivers are deemed to have consented to chemical tests when they apply for or renew a license; refusal brings a suspension.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Alcohol and drugs'

questions.q: What is the license suspension for a first refusal to take a breath (chemical) test?
questions.explain: A first refusal brings an automatic one-year suspension; a second within seven years brings two years.
questions.ref: Michigan State Police OHSP, 'Impaired Driving Law' (michigan.gov/msp)

questions.q: A second chemical-test refusal within seven years results in a license suspension of:
questions.explain: A second refusal within seven years carries a two-year suspension.
questions.ref: Michigan State Police OHSP, 'Impaired Driving Law' (michigan.gov/msp)

questions.q: Which drink contains the same amount of alcohol as a 12-ounce can of beer?
questions.explain: A 12-oz beer, a 5-oz glass of wine and a 1.5-oz shot of whiskey contain the same amount of alcohol.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Alcohol and drugs'

questions.q: What is the only thing that sobers up a person who has been drinking?
questions.explain: Coffee, cold showers, exercise and fresh air do not work; only time sobers you up.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Alcohol and drugs'

questions.q: For a first operating-while-intoxicated offense with a BAC below .17, the maximum jail time is:
questions.explain: A first OWI below .17 can bring up to 93 days in jail, a $500 fine, and six points.
questions.ref: Michigan State Police OHSP, 'Impaired Driving Law' (michigan.gov/msp)

questions.q: For a first offense with a BAC of .17 or higher, which penalty can apply?
options: Up to 180 days in jail and mandatory completion of an alcohol treatment program
Up to 30 days in jail and no license action
questions.explain: High-BAC first offenses carry up to 180 days in jail, up to a $700 fine, up to a one-year suspension and mandatory treatment.
questions.ref: Michigan State Police OHSP, 'Impaired Driving Law' (michigan.gov/msp)

questions.q: Under Michigan law, the penalties for driving under the influence of marijuana are:
options: The same as for driving under the influence of alcohol
A civil infraction with no points
Only a fine for drivers under 21
Lower, because marijuana is legal for adults
questions.explain: Penalties match alcohol OWI: up to 93 days jail, up to $500 fine, suspension and six points.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Alcohol and drugs'

questions.q: Which of the following is illegal in Michigan, even for an adult 21 or older?
options: Smoking marijuana in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public road
Transporting 1 ounce of marijuana in a vehicle
Riding as a sober passenger with someone who has marijuana in the trunk
questions.explain: Drivers and passengers are prohibited from smoking marijuana in the passenger area of a vehicle on a public way.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Alcohol and drugs'

questions.q: Drivers with any amount of a Schedule 1 drug or cocaine in their body face:
options: The same fines and penalties as drunk drivers
A warning on the first offense
questions.explain: Operating with any presence of a Schedule 1 drug or cocaine is treated like drunk driving and carries six points.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: For a first drug conviction (even when not driving), how long is the driver's license suspended?
questions.explain: With no prior drug violations, the license is suspended six months; no restricted license during the first 30 days.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Alcohol and drugs'

questions.q: How long do points stay on your Michigan driving record?
options: Two years from the date of conviction
questions.explain: Points remain on the record for two years from the conviction date.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: Accumulating how many points within two years requires a driver assessment reexamination?
questions.explain: Twelve or more points within two years (or six or more one-point violations) triggers a driver assessment reexamination.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for driving 16 mph or more over the legal speed limit (outside a work zone)?
questions.explain: Speeding 16 mph or more over the limit is a four-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for driving 6 to 10 mph over the speed limit (outside a work zone)?
questions.explain: 6-10 mph over is a two-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: Reckless driving carries how many points?
questions.explain: Reckless driving is a six-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: Failing to stop for a school bus carries how many points?
questions.explain: Failure to stop for a school bus or disobeying a school crossing guard is a three-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: Having an open alcohol container in the vehicle is a violation worth how many points?
questions.explain: An open container in a vehicle carries two points.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: How long does a conviction for impaired driving remain on your Michigan driving record?
questions.explain: Most convictions stay at least seven years, but fatality and impaired-driving convictions stay permanently.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Your driving record'

questions.q: Which statement about Michigan's point system is correct?
options: Insurance companies set the points on your state record
Points are posted when a ticket is written, even if dismissed
Points are posted only after you are convicted of a moving violation
questions.explain: Points go on your record only after conviction and are separate from insurance company points.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Michigan's point system'

questions.q: Which of these can lead to a driver reexamination?
options: Three or more crashes resulting in injury or property damage within two years
questions.explain: Three or more crashes in two years, 12+ points in two years, or violating license restrictions can lead to reexamination.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Driver reexaminations'

questions.q: If someone you know has been drinking and plans to drive, what is the best action?
options: Do not let them drive; arrange a sober driver, taxi or place to stay
Let them drive if they drink coffee first
Let them drive slowly on back roads
Follow them in your own car
questions.explain: Never let someone who has been drinking drive; take their keys if needed and find other transportation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 2, 'Alcohol and drugs'

questions.q: Michigan's Basic Speed Law requires you to drive:
options: At the speed of surrounding traffic, even above the limit
At exactly the posted speed limit at all times
No slower than 10 mph below the limit
At a careful and prudent speed that lets you stop within the clear distance ahead
questions.explain: You must drive at a careful and prudent speed—never above the limit and slower when conditions require.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Speed limits'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed on Michigan freeways?
questions.explain: Freeways are 70 mph maximum unless posted otherwise.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Speed limits'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the minimum speed on Michigan freeways?
questions.explain: Freeways have a 55 mph minimum unless posted otherwise.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Speed limits'

questions.q: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on Michigan highways and streets that are not freeways?
questions.explain: The default limit on non-freeway highways and streets is 55 mph unless posted.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Speed limits'

questions.q: What is the standard speed limit in a platted subdivision or condominium complex?
questions.explain: Platted subdivisions and condominium complexes have a 25 mph limit.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Speed limits'

questions.q: What is the standard speed limit in mobile home parks?
questions.explain: Mobile home parks and some municipal parks have a 15 mph limit.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Speed limits'

questions.q: On a Michigan freeway posted at 70 mph, school buses and trucks are limited to:
questions.explain: School buses and trucks are limited to 65 mph on 70 mph freeways and to 55 mph where the freeway limit is lower.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Speed limits'

questions.q: When a work zone is posted for 45 mph, what does that mean?
options: You may drive 45 mph only in the left lane
The speed limit in the work zone is 45 mph
questions.explain: For most construction work the limit is 45 mph when posted; if not posted for 45, the normal limit applies.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Construction zones'

questions.q: A 'Where Workers Present 45' sign means you should:
options: Drive 45 mph faster than workers' vehicles
Ignore the sign if you do not see equipment
Slow to 45 mph or less where workers are present; the normal limit may apply when they are absent
Always drive 45 mph through the entire zone, day or night
questions.explain: Some work zones limit speeds to 45 mph only when workers are present, returning to the normal limit otherwise.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Construction zones'

questions.q: Fines for moving violations in Michigan work zones are:
options: Waived if no workers are present
questions.explain: All moving-violation fines are doubled in work zones.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Construction zones'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding 10 mph or less over the limit in a work zone?
questions.explain: Work zone speeding carries increased points: 3 points for 10 mph or less over.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Construction zones'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding more than 15 mph over the limit in a work zone?
questions.explain: Work zone speeding more than 15 mph over the limit is a five-point violation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Construction zones'

questions.q: Causing injury or death to a person in a work zone can lead to a fine of up to:
options: $7,500 and up to 15 years in prison
questions.explain: Injuring or killing someone in a work zone can bring fines up to $7,500 and imprisonment up to 15 years.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Construction zones'

questions.q: What following distance does the Michigan handbook recommend under normal conditions?
questions.explain: A 3- to 4-second following distance is required; count from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Stopping distances'

questions.q: At higher speeds or in poor conditions, you should increase your following distance up to:
questions.explain: At higher speeds or in adverse conditions, increase following distance to 6 seconds or more if necessary.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Stopping distances'

questions.q: How should you measure your following distance?
options: Count seconds from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object until you reach it
Use your speedometer reading divided by ten
Stay close enough to read the vehicle's license plate
Count car lengths between you and the vehicle ahead
questions.explain: Pick a stationary point; if you reach it before counting 3 seconds, you are following too closely.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Stopping distances'

questions.q: In the quarter second it takes the brain to shift attention, how far does a car at 65 mph travel?
questions.explain: At 65 mph a car covers roughly 24 feet in a quarter second.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Distracted driving'

questions.q: A passenger vehicle at 55 mph can stop in about 130 feet. About how far does a loaded commercial truck need at the same speed?
questions.explain: A commercial vehicle at 55 mph needs about 400 feet to stop.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Commercial vehicles'

questions.q: How far ahead should you look while driving to spot hazards early?
options: Only at the vehicle directly in front
questions.explain: Look 20-30 seconds ahead to anticipate hazards and avoid last-second reactions.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Stopping distances'

questions.q: When following a horse and rider or a horse-drawn buggy, reduce your speed to about:
options: The posted limit and pass immediately
15-20 mph and stay at least 20 feet back
questions.explain: Slow to 15-20 mph and keep at least 20 feet away so you do not spook the horse.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Slow-moving vehicles'

questions.q: Slow-moving vehicles that display an orange triangle cannot travel faster than:
questions.explain: Slow-moving vehicles are those that cannot exceed 25 mph, such as farm machinery and Amish buggies.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Slow-moving vehicles'

questions.q: On a freeway with three or more lanes in your direction, if you are driving near the minimum speed you should:
options: Turn on your hazard lights and use any lane
Stay in the lane with the slower-moving traffic
questions.explain: On freeways with 3+ lanes you may use any lane, but slow drivers should stay with slower traffic.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Freeway driving'

questions.q: At a four-way stop, which vehicle goes first?
options: The vehicle on the busier road
The vehicle that arrived and stopped first
questions.explain: At an all-way stop the first driver to arrive and stop has the right of way.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. Who must yield?
options: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on its right
The vehicle on the right yields to the vehicle on its left
The vehicle going straight yields to the turning vehicle
questions.explain: When arriving together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: You reach an intersection where the traffic signal is not working and no officer is present. You must:
options: Treat it like a yield sign
Come to a complete stop and proceed as at a four-way stop
Proceed if you are on the larger road
Slow down and proceed if no one is coming
questions.explain: Stop completely, yield to vehicles already at the intersection, and yield to the right if arriving together.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: At a T-intersection with no signs or signals, who has the right of way?
options: Vehicles on the road that ends
questions.explain: At an uncontrolled T-intersection, yield to vehicles on the through road.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: Your light turns green but vehicles are still in the intersection. What should you do?
options: Proceed; your green gives you the right of way
Back up to give them room
questions.explain: If vehicles are still in the intersection when your light changes, you must yield before going.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: When turning left on a green light (no arrow), you must:
options: Expect oncoming traffic to stop for you
Wait for the light to turn yellow
Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then turn when clear
Turn before oncoming traffic starts moving
questions.explain: On a green ball you may turn left once oncoming traffic has cleared.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: In Michigan, may you turn left on a red light from a one-way street onto another one-way street?
options: Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
questions.explain: A left on red from one-way to one-way is allowed after a full stop and yielding to traffic.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way when turning'

questions.q: In Michigan, a left turn on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street is:
options: Allowed only with a green arrow
Allowed after a full stop, yielding to traffic and to opposite vehicles turning right
questions.explain: Michigan permits this turn after a full stop, scanning for traffic, and yielding to opposite right-turning vehicles.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: When turning right on a red light, you must:
options: Turn only if a green arrow appears
Stop completely and yield to pedestrians and other traffic
Slow down and turn if no cars are visible
questions.explain: Drivers turning right—including on red—must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way when turning'

questions.q: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: No one; entering traffic has priority
Traffic already in the roundabout, approaching from your left
questions.explain: Entering vehicles yield to traffic circulating counterclockwise, which approaches from the left.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: You are inside a roundabout and hear an emergency vehicle approaching. You should:
options: Continue to the nearest exit, then pull over to the right and stop
Speed up and stay in the circle
questions.explain: Do not stop in the roundabout; exit at the nearest exit and then pull over.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and siren approaches, you must:
options: Stop immediately where you are, even in an intersection
Pull to the right edge of the road, clear of intersections, and stop until it passes
Speed up to get out of its way
questions.explain: Drive to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of intersections, and stop until it has passed.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Emergency vehicles'

questions.q: How far must you stay behind a moving emergency vehicle that is using flashing lights and a siren?
questions.explain: Stay at least 500 feet behind a moving emergency vehicle displaying lights and siren.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Emergency vehicles'

questions.q: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, Michigan law requires you to:
options: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane
Slow to at least 10 mph below the posted limit and move over a lane if safe
questions.explain: The move-over law requires slowing at least 10 mph below the limit and changing lanes if conditions allow.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Emergency vehicles'

questions.q: Michigan's move-over law also covers which of these stopped vehicles with flashing lights?
options: Tow trucks, waste haulers, utility and road maintenance vehicles
questions.explain: Tow/road service vehicles count as emergency vehicles, and drivers must also use caution for waste, utility and maintenance vehicles.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Emergency vehicles'

questions.q: Failing to move over for a stopped emergency vehicle is a civil infraction unless:
options: Emergency personnel are injured or killed, which makes it a felony
questions.explain: Ordinarily it is a civil infraction, but injuring or killing emergency personnel makes it a felony.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Emergency vehicles'

questions.q: A funeral procession has the right of way over all vehicles except:
options: Fire trucks, ambulances and police vehicles
questions.explain: Funeral processions yield only to fire trucks, ambulances and police vehicles.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way and funerals'

questions.q: A pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk and your light is green. You must:
options: Proceed because you have a green light
questions.explain: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk even when your light is green.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way and pedestrians'

questions.q: You must stop or yield for a pedestrian who is using:
options: A crosswalk in another city only
A white cane or a guide dog
questions.explain: Michigan law requires drivers to stop or yield for pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: When approaching a MERGE sign, who must adjust speed to merge safely?
options: The vehicle in the left lane
questions.explain: The merging vehicle must yield and adjust its speed to merge safely with through traffic (MCL 257.649(7)).
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'A word about merging'

questions.q: At an intersection with a flashing yellow arrow, you may turn:
options: Without yielding, because the arrow protects you
Only after coming to a full stop and waiting for green
After yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
questions.explain: A flashing yellow arrow permits a turn after yielding to oncoming traffic, pedestrians and bicyclists.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: In the middle of the intersection
Ten car lengths before the sign
At a point where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection
Anywhere, as long as you slow down
questions.explain: Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop where you can see all approaching traffic without pulling into the intersection.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Right of way at intersections'

questions.q: Whose directions take priority over traffic signals and signs?
options: The driver with the larger vehicle
A law enforcement officer's (and in work zones, a construction worker's)
questions.explain: Always obey an officer's orders; construction workers directing traffic must also be obeyed even if they conflict with signals.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'In conclusion'

questions.q: You are approaching a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross. You should:
options: Stop as well; never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian
Honk to let the pedestrian know you are coming
Pass it carefully on the left
questions.explain: Never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian; the stopped vehicle may hide the pedestrian.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: When passing on a two-lane road, you must return to your lane before coming within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle?
questions.explain: You must return to your lane before you are within 200 feet of any oncoming vehicle.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Passing on the left'

questions.q: Passing is prohibited within how many feet of an intersection or railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Do not pass within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'When passing is prohibited'

questions.q: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: As soon as your rear bumper clears its front bumper
When you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror
When the other driver flashes headlights
questions.explain: Do not cut back in until the whole vehicle you passed is visible in your rearview mirror.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Passing on the left'

questions.q: Which is a situation where passing on the right is allowed?
options: Whenever the driver ahead is going under the limit
Using the paved shoulder on a two-lane road
On any two-lane road if no one is oncoming
On a one-way street with more than one lane
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed on multi-lane one-way streets, roads with 2+ lanes each way, or when the vehicle ahead turns left and there is room—never using the shoulder.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Passing on the right'

questions.q: Which is NOT a place where passing is prohibited?
options: Where a solid yellow line is on your side of the center line
When approaching a hill or curve that blocks your view
On a straight road with a broken yellow center line and clear view ahead
When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing
questions.explain: A broken yellow line with clear visibility permits passing when safe; the other situations prohibit it.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'When passing is prohibited'

questions.q: You are passing on a two-lane road and your view is blocked within 100 feet of a:
options: Bridge, viaduct or tunnel—so you must not pass
questions.explain: Passing is prohibited when your view is obstructed within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'When passing is prohibited'

questions.q: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: Speed up to stay even with it
Move to the left to block it
Maintain or reduce speed and let it complete the pass
questions.explain: Never increase your speed or race a driver who is passing you.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Passing on the left'

questions.q: The center lane of a three-lane road is marked for left turns only. You may use it to:
options: Travel when the right lane is busy
Merge into traffic over a long distance
questions.explain: Using a left-turn-only center lane for passing or merging is prohibited.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Left turn only center lane'

questions.q: When driving on a Michigan interstate or full-access-controlled freeway, which lane should you normally use?
options: The right-hand lane, except for permitted reasons such as passing
questions.explain: On interstates and controlled freeways you must drive in the right lane except for listed exceptions.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Lane usage'

questions.q: On a two-lane freeway, which is a valid reason to drive in the left lane?
options: Preparing to exit right in five miles
Allowing another vehicle to merge onto the freeway
questions.explain: Use the left lane on a two-lane freeway for passing, left exits, letting vehicles merge, congestion, or emergency/construction on the shoulder.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Freeway driving'

questions.q: To use a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane during its hours of operation, a car must carry at least:
questions.explain: HOV lanes require two or more occupants during peak hours; motorcycles may use them any time.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Freeway driving'

questions.q: You miss your freeway exit. What should you do?
options: Continue to the next exit and come back
Use the median crossover to turn around
Stop and wait for a gap to reverse
questions.explain: Do not reverse, turn around or cut across the median; go on to the next exit and come back.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Leaving a freeway'

questions.q: Who may use the emergency crossover in a freeway median?
options: Only authorized emergency, police and MDOT/maintenance vehicles
Any driver who missed an exit
questions.explain: Median crossovers are only for emergency and Michigan Department of Transportation vehicles.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Leaving a freeway'

questions.q: How is a 'Michigan Left' made?
options: Go straight or turn right, then make a U-turn at a designated median crossover
Turn left directly from the right lane
Make a left turn on any red light
questions.explain: Michigan Lefts prohibit direct left turns; drivers pass the intersection (or turn right) and use a median crossover.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Michigan Lefts'

questions.q: An unmarked median crossover used for a Michigan Left should be treated as:
options: A single-lane crossover, one vehicle at a time
questions.explain: Extra width is for large vehicles; unless marked for two lanes, treat a crossover as single-lane.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Michigan Lefts'

questions.q: When there are two left-turn lanes, you should:
options: Finish your turn in the lane that corresponds to your turn lane
Turn into any lane that is open
Cross into the far lane to pass
Always finish in the right lane
questions.explain: With multiple turn lanes, complete the turn into the corresponding lane to avoid cutting others off.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Turning'

questions.q: While waiting to make a left turn, keep your front wheels:
options: Pointed straight ahead until you begin the turn
Turned left so you are ready
questions.explain: Straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Turning'

questions.q: When making a right turn, you should:
options: Swing wide into the left lane first
Not signal if no one is behind you
Follow the curve of the curb and stay in your lane
questions.explain: Turn from the correct lane, signal, and follow the general curve of the curb.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Turning'

questions.q: Before changing lanes to the left, you should:
options: Check mirrors, do a head check over your left shoulder, and signal
Signal while moving over at the same time
questions.explain: Look behind and to the left with a head check, signal, then move carefully.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Changing lanes'

questions.q: Which is a reason you may drive left of the center line on a two-way road?
options: To pass an obstruction when the way is clear, yielding to oncoming traffic
To avoid potholes on a curve without checking
questions.explain: You may cross the center line around stopped vehicles or obstacles, but must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Lane usage'

questions.q: Weaving from lane to lane to speed through traffic is:
questions.explain: Michigan law forbids darting between lanes to get ahead of other traffic.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Lane usage'

questions.q: When should you use your turn signal before turning?
options: Only when other vehicles are visible
Always, for every turn and lane change
questions.explain: Always use your turn signal when turning.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Turning'

questions.q: Which hand signal is shown by the left arm extended straight out?
questions.explain: Left arm straight out signals a left turn; arm up signals right; arm down signals stop.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Turning'

questions.q: Inside a roundabout, you should:
options: Pass slower vehicles on the left
Turn left to reach your exit faster
Avoid changing lanes and choose your lane before entering
questions.explain: Choose the correct lane before entering; avoid lane changes and passing in the roundabout.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: When is it legal to drive across a freeway median strip?
options: When oncoming traffic is light and visibility is good
Never, unless you are an authorized emergency vehicle
questions.explain: Driving over a freeway median or through a barrier is against the law; freeway crossovers are for emergency and MDOT vehicles only.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Lane usage'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
questions.explain: Never park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking violations'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a marked crosswalk?
questions.explain: Do not park within 20 feet of a marked crosswalk (or 15 feet of an intersection with no crosswalk).
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking violations'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a stop sign, traffic light or flashing beacon?
questions.explain: Parking is prohibited within 30 feet of a stop sign, traffic signal or flashing beacon.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking violations'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: Do not park within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking violations'

questions.q: On the same side of the street, you may not park within how many feet of a fire station driveway?
questions.explain: Stay 20 feet from a fire station driveway on the same side (75 feet on the opposite side when marked).
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking violations'

questions.q: You may not park within how many feet of a fire or a crash?
questions.explain: Never park within 500 feet of a fire or crash.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking violations'

questions.q: When parallel parked, your vehicle must be no more than how far from the curb?
questions.explain: Parking more than 12 inches from the curb is prohibited; aim for 6-12 inches.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking violations'

questions.q: When parking downhill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
options: Toward the center of the road
questions.explain: Turn wheels toward the curb when parking downhill.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking on a hill'

questions.q: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels:
options: It does not matter if the brake is set
questions.explain: Turn wheels away from the curb when parking uphill.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking on a hill'

questions.q: When parking on a hill with no curb, turn your wheels:
options: So the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves
Toward the center of the road
questions.explain: With no curb, turn the wheels so the vehicle will not roll into traffic.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking on a hill'

questions.q: Whenever you park, you should:
options: Leave the engine running for security
Leave the keys in the ignition for valets
Set the parking brake and not rely on the transmission to hold the vehicle
questions.explain: Always set the parking brake, turn off the engine and take the keys.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking'

questions.q: When starting to parallel park, how far from the parked vehicle ahead of the space should you pull alongside?
options: As close as possible without touching
questions.explain: Pull alongside the vehicle ahead of the space with 2-5 feet between the vehicles.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parallel parking'

questions.q: To park in a disability parking space, you must:
options: Have a disability plate or placard and the person with the disability must be with you
questions.explain: A qualifying disability and a disability plate or placard are required; the person must be accompanying you.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Disability parking'

questions.q: Which vehicles receive free metered parking in Michigan?
options: Those displaying a disability placard with a yellow free-parking sticker
Any vehicle with a disability plate
questions.explain: Only placards with a yellow free-parking sticker get free parking.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Disability parking'

questions.q: Why must you never park on the blue-striped area beside a van-accessible space?
options: It is a loading zone for deliveries
It is needed for a wheelchair lift or ramp
It is a fire lane for trucks
questions.explain: The striped area gives room for a van's wheelchair lift and ramp.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Van-accessible disability parking'

questions.q: Before opening your door after parking on a street, what technique helps you spot cyclists?
options: Open the door quickly to reduce exposure
Rely only on the side mirror
Open the door with your right hand so you naturally look over your left shoulder
questions.explain: Using the right hand turns your body so you look back for cyclists and pedestrians.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Parking'

questions.q: When passing a bicyclist, Michigan law requires at least how much space?
questions.explain: You must leave at least 3 feet when passing a bicyclist (some cities require 5).
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: May you pass a bicyclist in a no-passing zone in Michigan?
options: Yes, if it is safe to do so
Only if the cyclist waves you on
questions.explain: The handbook allows passing a bicyclist in a no-passing zone when it is safe.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Bicyclists in Michigan may legally ride on:
questions.explain: Cyclists may use any Michigan road other than limited-access freeways, with the same rights and duties as drivers.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Are bicyclists required to ride in an available bicycle lane?
options: No; they may leave it to turn left or avoid hazards
questions.explain: Bicyclists are not required to use a bike lane.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: A green-painted bicycle lane indicates:
options: A potential conflict point between cars and bicycles
A lane open to cars on weekends
A lane drivers may use for right turns
questions.explain: Green bike lanes mark conflict points; it is illegal to drive, turn or park in bike lanes.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Bicycle lanes'

questions.q: What following distance should you keep behind a motorcycle, scooter or bicycle?
questions.explain: Tailgating is illegal; leave at least 3-4 seconds behind motorcyclists and cyclists.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Motorcycles, scooters, mopeds and bicycles'

questions.q: Driving beside a motorcyclist in the same lane is:
options: Illegal; pass using an adjacent lane
Legal if the lane is wide
questions.explain: You may not share a lane with a motorcycle or pass one within its lane; use the next lane when it is legal and safe.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Specifically about motorcyclists'

questions.q: Why should you leave extra space behind a motorcyclist in city traffic?
options: Motorcyclists often slow by downshifting, which does not turn on the brake light
It is required only at night
questions.explain: Engine braking and downshifting slow a motorcycle without activating brake lights.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Specifically about motorcyclists'

questions.q: Where do most vehicle-motorcycle crashes occur?
options: At intersections and on busy city streets
questions.explain: Intersections are among the highest-risk locations for crashes with motorcycles.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Specifically about motorcyclists'

questions.q: Motorcycles may legally use freeways if their engine size is:
questions.explain: Motorcycles of 125cc or more may use freeways; 124cc or less may not.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Specifically about motorcyclists'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT allowed on Michigan freeways?
questions.explain: Pedestrians, small motorcycles (124cc or less), mopeds, bicycles, ATVs and slow-moving vehicles are not allowed on freeways.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Freeway driving'

questions.q: When you see a commercial truck signaling a right turn at an intersection, expect it to:
options: Swing wide to the left before turning right
Turn sharply from the right lane
questions.explain: Trucks may swing wide to the left to make a right turn—do not squeeze in on the right.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Commercial vehicles'

questions.q: Why is it important to stop behind the white stop line at intersections when trucks are turning?
options: A turning truck may need that space and could hit you
It helps pedestrians see your plate
Stopping past the line gives you a better view
questions.explain: If you stop past the line, a truck may be unable to complete its turn without hitting you.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Commercial vehicles'

questions.q: The areas around a large truck where the driver cannot see you are called:
questions.explain: Trucks have large blind spots called 'no zones' where you should not linger.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Commercial vehicles'

questions.q: After passing a large truck, when should you move back in front of it?
options: When you can see the entire cab in your rearview mirror
Immediately after your car clears its bumper
questions.explain: Signal and pull back only when the whole cab is visible in your rearview mirror.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Passing a commercial vehicle safely'

questions.q: When following a truck or bus at night, use:
questions.explain: Use low beams when following a truck or bus at night.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Commercial vehicles'

questions.q: You are behind a truck that is backing up. You should:
questions.explain: Do not pass behind a truck that is backing; an 8.5-foot-wide trailer can block the driver's view of your car.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Commercial vehicles'

questions.q: When a large truck or bus is passing you in bad weather, you should:
options: Slow down and start your wipers before spray reduces visibility
questions.explain: Splash and spray can reduce visibility; slow down and start your wipers early.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Passing a commercial vehicle safely'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT considered a slow-moving vehicle?
questions.explain: Golf carts and four-wheel ATVs do not count as slow-moving vehicles under the handbook.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Slow-moving vehicles'

questions.q: If a street has no sidewalk, pedestrians walking along the road should:
options: Walk in the center of the lane
Walk with their back to traffic
questions.explain: Pedestrians walking along a road without sidewalks should face oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: Near a person who is blind or visually impaired, you should avoid:
questions.explain: Noise covers audible cues used by people with visual impairments.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: Before turning right at an intersection, you should check for:
options: Only pedestrians on the far corner
Only cars in the left lane
Bicyclists coming from behind on the shoulder or in a bike lane
Nothing if your light is green
questions.explain: Look for cyclists approaching from behind on your right and yield before turning.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Why is it hard to judge an approaching motorcycle's speed and distance?
options: Motorcycles are always louder than cars
Its single headlight and small profile make it seem farther away and slower
questions.explain: A motorcycle's small profile can distort your perception, making it seem you have more time than you do.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Specifically about motorcyclists'

questions.q: When should you be especially watchful for children?
options: Near parked cars, school zones, playgrounds and parks
questions.explain: Children are unpredictable and may dart into the street near these locations.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Children'

questions.q: Under Michigan's cell phone law (effective for all drivers), which is illegal while driving?
options: A single tap to answer in hands-free mode
Holding a phone to make a call or read a text
Using a GPS without entering data by hand
questions.explain: Michigan prohibits holding or manually using a mobile device while driving; limited hands-free use is allowed.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Cell phone use prohibited for all drivers – including teens'

questions.q: What is the fine for a first violation of Michigan's hand-held phone law?
questions.explain: The fine is $100 for a first offense and $250 for subsequent violations.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Distracted driving'

questions.q: When may any driver, including a teen, use a mobile device while driving?
options: To report a crash, crime, medical emergency or dangerous driver to 9-1-1 or emergency services
To text a parent that they are running late
To check social media at a red light
To record a video of traffic
questions.explain: Emergency exceptions allow calling or texting 9-1-1 or emergency services to report emergencies.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Cell phone use prohibited for all drivers – including teens'

questions.q: Under Michigan's seat belt law, who must be buckled up?
options: The driver, all front-seat passengers, and all passengers under 16 in any seat
questions.explain: All front-seat occupants and all passengers under 16 in every seat must be buckled.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Buckle up, it's the law!'

questions.q: Children must ride in a car seat or booster seat until they are:
options: 8 years old or 4 feet 9 inches tall
questions.explain: A child restraint is required until age 8 or 4'9", whichever comes first.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Protecting children and teens'

questions.q: Children younger than what age must ride in a rear seat if the vehicle has one available?
questions.explain: Children under 4 must be in a rear seat if available (unless all rear seats are occupied by children under 4).
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Protecting children and teens'

questions.q: A child in a rear-facing car seat may ride in the front seat only if:
options: The child is over 1 year old
The front passenger air bag is turned off
questions.explain: Rear-facing seats may be placed in front only if the passenger air bag is deactivated.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Protecting children and teens'

questions.q: Anyone under 18 may not ride in the open bed of a pickup truck traveling faster than:
questions.explain: Riding in an open pickup bed over 15 mph is prohibited for those under 18, with limited exceptions.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Protecting children and teens'

questions.q: It is illegal to leave a child unattended in a vehicle if the child is younger than:
options: 6 years old and the situation poses an unreasonable risk
questions.explain: Children under 6 may not be left unattended when it creates an unreasonable risk; supervision by someone 13+ is allowed.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Children left unattended in vehicles'

questions.q: How far should the center of your breastbone be from the center of the steering wheel?
questions.explain: Sit with at least 10 inches between your breastbone and the steering wheel air bag.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Air bags'

questions.q: When are headlights required in Michigan?
options: From sunset to sunrise only on freeways
From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and whenever you cannot see clearly 500 feet ahead
questions.explain: Headlights must be on from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and any time visibility is under 500 feet.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Driving at night'

questions.q: You must dim your high beams within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle?
questions.explain: It is illegal to use or flash high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Driving at night'

questions.q: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?
options: Toward the right edge of the road ahead
questions.explain: Look at the right edge of your lane to avoid being blinded by glare.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Driving at night'

questions.q: When driving in fog, you should use:
questions.explain: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Rain and fog'

questions.q: If fog becomes so thick you cannot see, you should:
options: Pull off the road, turn on hazard flashers and wait
Turn on your high beams and keep going
questions.explain: Pull completely off the road, use four-way flashers and wait for the fog to lift.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Rain and fog'

questions.q: When are roads most slippery after it starts to rain?
options: After it has rained for three hours
questions.explain: Oil on the pavement makes roads most slippery in the first half hour of rain.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Rain and fog'

questions.q: On wet roads, how much should you increase your following distance?
options: At least twice the normal distance
questions.explain: Slow down and allow at least twice the normal following distance in rain.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Rain and fog'

questions.q: What contributes to hydroplaning?
options: Worn tires, low tire pressure and driving too fast on wet roads
questions.explain: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water; worn tires, low pressure and speed contribute.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Rain and fog'

questions.q: After driving through deep water, you should:
options: Speed up to dry the brakes
Test your brakes by gently pressing the pedal until they work normally
questions.explain: Wet brakes may pull or fail; slow down and lightly apply them until they work properly.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Rain and fog'

questions.q: In cold weather, which part of the road freezes first?
questions.explain: Bridges and underpasses freeze before the road surface does.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Bad weather'

questions.q: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do first?
options: Take your foot off the accelerator and steer where you want to go
questions.explain: Ease off the gas, steer only enough to point the wheels where you want to go, and be ready for a secondary skid.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If your vehicle begins skidding'

questions.q: In an emergency stop with anti-lock brakes (ABS), you should:
options: Release the brake when it vibrates
Apply firm, hard pressure and hold it until stopped
questions.explain: With ABS, brake hard and maintain pressure; vibration or pulsing is normal.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Braking'

questions.q: Without anti-lock brakes, how should you stop hard on a slippery road?
options: Slam the brake and hold it
Brake just hard enough not to lock the wheels; if they lock, release and reapply
questions.explain: This 'threshold' or controlled braking keeps the wheels turning so you can steer.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Braking'

questions.q: On long trips, how often should you take a break to fight fatigue?
questions.explain: Stop for a 10-minute break at least every two hours; do not rely on coffee or stay-awake drugs.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Freeway fatigue'

questions.q: An oncoming vehicle is in your lane. Which way should you try to escape?
options: To the right edge of the road
questions.explain: Look for an escape route to the right; the other driver may return to their own lane.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane'

questions.q: When a deer crash seems unavoidable, you should:
options: Flash your high beams and honk continuously
Brake firmly, hold the wheel and stay in your lane
questions.explain: Don't veer for deer—brake firmly, hold on with both hands and come to a controlled stop.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If a vehicle-deer crash is unavoidable'

questions.q: When are deer crashes most likely?
options: At dawn and dusk, especially in fall and spring
questions.explain: Be especially alert at dawn and dusk and in fall and spring; deer often travel in groups.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Your best defense against deer'

questions.q: Which of these reduces the risk of hitting deer?
options: Slowing down when you see one deer because others may follow
questions.explain: Deer whistles, flashing lights and honking do not deter deer; expect more than one.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Your best defense against deer'

questions.q: Where do crashes cause more traffic fatalities and serious injuries than on any other part of the road?
questions.explain: Intersection crashes cause more fatalities and serious injuries than any other road location.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Take care at intersections'

questions.q: Your view at an intersection is blocked by a snowbank. You should:
options: Go quickly to minimize time exposed
Back up and choose another route
Edge forward slowly until you can see
questions.explain: Creep forward slowly until you can see past the obstruction.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Take care at intersections'

questions.q: If another driver is tailgating you, the handbook advises you to:
options: Move over or pull over and let them pass
questions.explain: It is safer to have tailgaters in front of you.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Are you an aggressive driver?'

questions.q: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:
options: Follow them to get their plate number
Get out of the way, avoid eye contact and report them if it is safe
questions.explain: Avoid confrontation; ignore gestures and call police if safe.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Are you an aggressive driver?'

questions.q: Most cars have blind spots located:
options: To the left rear and right rear of the vehicle
Directly in front of the hood
questions.explain: Blind spots are at the left and right rear; always do a head check before changing lanes.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Before starting the engine'

questions.q: Which is a good way to avoid in-vehicle distractions?
options: Set your navigation and music before you start driving
Eat a full meal while driving on freeways
Look up phone numbers at stop lights
questions.explain: Plan routes, preset radio and finish grooming before driving.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Distracted driving'

questions.q: If you are involved in a crash with no serious injury and your car can be driven, you should:
options: Drive home and report it later
Move it off the main roadway to a safe place such as the shoulder
Leave it in place until police arrive
Leave the scene if no one is hurt
questions.explain: Drivable vehicles in crashes without serious injury should be moved off the roadway when safe.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Crashes'

questions.q: You must notify police of a crash if there are injuries or property damage of more than:
questions.explain: Notify police if there are injuries or property damage exceeding $1,000.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Crashes'

questions.q: After a crash, what information must drivers exchange?
options: Names, addresses, driver's license numbers, registration and insurance
Nothing if police are not called
questions.explain: Exchange names, addresses, license numbers, registration and insurance information.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Crashes'

questions.q: Leaving the scene of a crash you are involved in is:
options: Illegal and punishable by fines, jail or both
Allowed if you leave a note
questions.explain: Never drive away from a crash; penalties increase with alcohol, injuries or deaths.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Crashes'

questions.q: If you hit a deer, who should you report it to?
options: Local police, the county sheriff, the State Police or the DNR
questions.explain: Report deer crashes to law enforcement or the DNR, who can issue a permit to keep the deer.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Vehicle – deer crashes'

questions.q: Your car becomes disabled on a busy road. The handbook recommends that you:
options: Get out and stand behind the car
Pull as far off the road as possible, turn on hazards and stay inside with your seat belt on
Leave the car in the travel lane
Walk along the freeway to find help
questions.explain: Generally, the safest place is in your car, buckled up, until help arrives.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If your car becomes disabled'

questions.q: If you must stop on a freeway because of an emergency, you should:
options: Back up to the last exit
Turn on hazard flashers, slow gradually and pull completely off the pavement
questions.explain: Never stop on a freeway except in an emergency, and then get fully off the pavement.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Leaving a freeway'

questions.q: When an officer signals you to pull over, you should:
options: Reach for your documents before the officer arrives
Get out and walk to the police car
Pull to the right side as soon as safe, stay in the car with hands visible on the wheel
questions.explain: Pull over safely, stay buckled in the car, keep hands visible and get documents only when asked.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If you are pulled over'

questions.q: If you disagree with a ticket you receive during a traffic stop, you should:
options: Discuss it with the court, not the officer
Argue with the officer at the scene
Refuse to sign or accept it
questions.explain: Do not argue at the stop; take up any dispute with the court.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If you are pulled over'
