questions.q: Your car stalls on railroad tracks and the crossing lights are flashing. What should you do?
options: Push the car off the tracks
Get everyone out immediately, move far away from the tracks and call 911
Stay in the car with seat belts on
questions.explain: If gates are activated or a train is coming, evacuate immediately and get far from the tracks.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'If you are stuck on the tracks'

questions.q: Your car is stuck on the tracks but no train is coming and signals are not active. After getting everyone out, you should:
options: Call the number on the blue Emergency Notification Sign and give the crossing ID
Wait in the car for a tow
Flag down a train with your hands
questions.explain: Call the railroad's emergency number on the blue ENS sign, give the crossing ID, then call 911.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'If you are stuck on the tracks'

questions.q: Once crossing lights and gates activate, about how long do you have before the train arrives?
questions.explain: You have roughly 20 seconds after activation or hearing the train horn.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'If you are stuck on the tracks'

questions.q: What information appears on a railroad Emergency Notification System (ENS) sign?
options: A phone number and the crossing's identification number
questions.explain: ENS signs list a phone number and the crossing ID (six digits and a letter) to report emergencies.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'What is an Emergency Notification System sign?'

questions.q: If someone acting suspiciously approaches your car, you should:
options: Keep doors locked and try to drive away or sound the horn
Roll down your window to talk
questions.explain: Drive away or sound the horn and stay inside the locked car.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If you are approached or threatened while in your car'

questions.q: Which is true about leaving your vehicle if it becomes disabled on a freeway?
options: Walk along the freeway shoulder to the next exit
Stand behind the car to warn traffic
Walking on the freeway is dangerous and illegal; go directly to a safe place far from traffic
Cross the freeway to get help
questions.explain: If you must leave, move to a safe location away from the roadway; walking on freeways is illegal.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'If your car becomes disabled'

questions.q: A diamond-shaped sign is used for:
questions.explain: Diamond signs warn of hazards or changes ahead.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic signs'

questions.q: A five-sided (pentagon) sign indicates:
options: A school zone or school crossing
questions.explain: Pentagon-shaped signs mark school areas and crossings.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic signs'

questions.q: Orange signs are used for:
options: Services such as gas and food
questions.explain: Orange indicates caution for construction or maintenance.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign colors'

questions.q: Blue road signs give information about:
options: Services such as gas, food, lodging or hospitals
questions.explain: Blue signs indicate services and hospitality.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign colors'

questions.q: Fluorescent pink signs are used for:
questions.explain: Fluorescent pink marks incident management and unplanned events.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign colors'

questions.q: White lines on the pavement separate:
options: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction
questions.explain: White lines separate same-direction lanes; yellow lines separate opposite directions.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Pavement markings'

questions.q: Yellow lines on the pavement separate:
options: Traffic moving in the same direction
questions.explain: Yellow lines divide traffic flowing in opposite directions.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Yellow lines'

questions.q: A double solid white line between lanes means:
options: Travel in the same direction on both sides, but crossing the line is prohibited
questions.explain: Do not cross double solid white lines.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Double solid white lines'

questions.q: White triangles painted across a lane (a yield line) mean:
options: Be ready to stop and yield to pedestrians
questions.explain: White triangle yield lines show where to stop when yielding to pedestrians.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Yield lines'

questions.q: A steady red arrow means:
options: Stop; you may not turn in that direction until the signal changes
questions.explain: A solid red arrow requires a stop; no turning until it changes.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Flashing yellow arrow left-turn signal head'

questions.q: Flashing green lights on a state or local road maintenance vehicle mean:
options: Road work is taking place; slow down and use caution
You may pass at full speed
questions.explain: Maintenance vehicles may display green lights when working; slow down.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Maintenance vehicles'

questions.q: What must you do at this sign?
options: Stop fully, then let traffic and pedestrians go first before you continue
Stop only if cross traffic is present
Slow down and proceed if clear
questions.explain: A STOP sign requires a full stop and yielding before proceeding.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign require?
options: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let crossing traffic go first
Come to a full stop every time
questions.explain: A YIELD sign means slow and give right of way to crossing traffic; stop if necessary.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not enter this road from your direction
questions.explain: DO NOT ENTER marks roads or ramps you are not allowed to enter.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: You see this sign facing you. What should you do?
options: You are heading into oncoming traffic; leave the roadway as quickly and safely as you can
Continue carefully to the next exit
Stop in the lane and wait
questions.explain: A WRONG WAY sign facing you means you are driving against traffic and must get out of that lane at once, safely.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign mean at an intersection?
options: You may turn right on red without stopping
You may not turn while the signal is red
questions.explain: NO TURN ON RED prohibits turning on a red light; wait for green.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Turn only in the direction of the arrow at the next corner
All traffic on this road flows in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: ONE WAY means traffic in all lanes moves the same direction.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: DO NOT PASS prohibits passing in that area.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The no-passing zone has ended; pass only when it is safe
questions.explain: PASS WITH CARE marks the end of a no-passing zone.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Oncoming traffic must yield to you
On a green ball, you may turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic
You have a protected left turn on green
Left turns are prohibited on green
questions.explain: LEFT TURN YIELD ON GREEN means the left turn is permissive, not protected.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic signals'

questions.q: What does this sign mark?
options: A railroad crossing; look, listen and yield to trains
An intersection with a four-way stop
questions.explain: The white X crossbuck marks a highway-rail grade crossing.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Passive railroad crossing control systems'

questions.q: After passing this sign, a train is approaching the crossing. Where must you stop?
options: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
questions.explain: All vehicles must stop no more than 50 feet and no less than 15 feet from the tracks.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Railroad crossing advance warning sign'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: The road curves one way and then the other
questions.explain: This is a reverse curve warning; the road bends one way then the other.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: An intersection ahead; watch for cross traffic
questions.explain: The cross symbol warns that a road intersects ahead.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: Traffic will be merging from the right
questions.explain: This sign warns that traffic merges into your road from the right.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The right lane ends; merge left and yield to traffic in the left lane
questions.explain: LANE ENDS MERGE LEFT: the right lane is ending; yield to traffic in the left lane.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: The divided highway ends; traffic will travel in both directions without a median
questions.explain: DIVIDED HIGHWAY ENDS means the road becomes two-way without separation.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: TWO-WAY TRAFFIC warns that opposing traffic shares the road ahead.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
questions.explain: STOP AHEAD warns that you will soon need to stop.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: The road becomes slippery when wet; drive carefully
questions.explain: SLIPPERY WHEN WET warns of reduced traction in rain or bad weather.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this sign warn of?
options: A steep downgrade ahead; check your brakes and use a lower gear if needed
questions.explain: The HILL sign warns of a steep downslope, especially important for large trucks.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this five-sided sign warn of?
options: A school zone or school crossing; watch for children and obey crossing guards
questions.explain: The pentagon school sign marks school children present; obey crossing guards.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this sign, especially at dawn or dusk?
options: Flash your high beams to scare deer
Slow down and watch for deer, which often travel in groups
questions.explain: Deer crossing signs mark high-risk areas; slow down and stay alert.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 7, 'Your best defense against deer'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: The maximum clearance under the structure ahead is 12 feet 6 inches
The road is 12 feet 6 inches wide
questions.explain: This sign gives the maximum height allowed under a bridge or structure.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: Where is this pennant-shaped sign posted and what does it mean?
options: On the left side of the road; it marks the start of a no-passing zone
On the right side; merge ahead
On the right side; passing allowed
questions.explain: The NO PASSING ZONE pennant is placed on the left side of the road.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: This yellow plaque appears under a curve warning sign. What does it mean?
options: The speed limit for the whole road is 35 mph
The legal minimum speed is 35 mph
The recommended safe speed for the curve is 35 mph
questions.explain: Advisory speed plaques give a recommended speed for the hazard ahead.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: What does this orange sign mean?
options: Construction or maintenance crews may be working ahead; drive with care
questions.explain: ROAD WORK AHEAD warns of a work zone; fines are doubled there.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic sign challenge answers'

questions.q: This orange triangle with a red border on the back of a vehicle means:
options: The vehicle is an emergency vehicle
The vehicle cannot travel faster than 25 mph
questions.explain: The slow-moving vehicle emblem marks vehicles that cannot exceed 25 mph.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 6, 'Slow-moving vehicles'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: Stop and wait for a green light
Slow down and proceed without stopping
The signal is about to turn green
Come to a full stop, then proceed when the way is clear
questions.explain: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Flashing red light'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: Proceed carefully through the intersection, watching for cross traffic
The signal is broken; treat as a four-way stop
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Flashing yellow light'

questions.q: You are approaching this signal and can stop safely before the intersection. What must you do?
options: Speed up to clear the intersection
Proceed if no one is coming
questions.explain: Michigan requires stopping on yellow when you can do so safely.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Traffic signals'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: Turn left only after oncoming traffic clears
Oncoming traffic is stopped and you may turn left, yielding to pedestrians in the crosswalk
questions.explain: A steady green arrow gives a protected turn; still yield to pedestrians.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Steady green arrow'

questions.q: What do these center-line markings mean?
options: Passing allowed only for the side with the broken line
questions.explain: A double solid yellow line prohibits passing for traffic in both directions.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Solid yellow lines'

questions.q: Under these markings, which driver may pass?
options: Only the driver on the side with the broken line, when safe
Only the driver on the side with the solid line
questions.explain: If the solid yellow line is on your side, you may not cross it to pass.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Solid yellow lines'

questions.q: What do these markings indicate?
options: A merge lane for entering traffic
A center lane reserved for left turns by traffic from either direction
questions.explain: Left-turn-only center lanes have solid outer and broken inner yellow lines; do not use them to pass.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 5, 'Left turn only center lane'

questions.q: A school bus ahead has its red overhead lights flashing. You must stop at least how far from the bus?
questions.explain: Stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red overhead lights.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'School buses'

questions.q: How long must you remain stopped for a school bus with flashing red lights?
options: Until the red lights stop flashing or the bus moves on
Until the driver waves you on
questions.explain: Stay stopped until the red lights are turned off or the bus resumes travel.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'School buses'

questions.q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on the other side of a road divided by a grass median. You:
options: Must stop at least 20 feet away
Must stop only if children are visible
questions.explain: No stop is needed for a bus on the other side of a highway divided by a barrier or median.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'School buses'

questions.q: A school bus's yellow overhead lights are flashing. This means:
options: Prepare to stop; the bus is about to stop to load or unload
questions.explain: Flashing yellow overhead lights mean prepare to stop.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'School bus signals'

questions.q: A school bus is showing its yellow hazard warning lights. You should:
options: Stop until the lights go off
questions.explain: Yellow hazard lights on a bus mean proceed with caution.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'School bus signals'

questions.q: Fines for failing to stop for a school bus are:
options: Double the normal fine for a moving violation
The same as a parking ticket
questions.explain: Fines for failing to stop for a school bus are doubled.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'School buses'

questions.q: Which vehicles must stop at railroad crossings even when no train is visible and no signal is active (unless marked otherwise)?
options: School buses, vehicles carrying passengers for hire, and hazardous-material vehicles
questions.explain: School buses, for-hire passenger vehicles, gasoline trucks and hazmat carriers must stop at crossings.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Railroad crossings'

questions.q: At a railroad crossing with a stop sign, you must:
options: Stop only if a train is coming
Stop whether or not a train is in sight
questions.explain: A stop sign at a crossing requires a stop even with no train visible.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Railroad crossings'

questions.q: After a train passes a crossing with gates, when may you proceed?
options: When the gates begin to rise
When the gates are up, lights stop flashing, bells stop and all tracks are clear
As soon as the last car passes
When the car ahead drives around the gate
questions.explain: Wait until gates rise, signals and bells stop, and you are sure all tracks are clear.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Railroad crossings'

questions.q: Traffic is backed up on the far side of a railroad crossing. You should not cross unless:
options: There is room for your vehicle to clear the far side of the tracks by at least 6 feet
You can partially clear the tracks
questions.explain: Never cross unless your vehicle can completely clear the far side by at least 6 feet.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Trains and vehicles DO NOT MIX: Grade crossing safety tips'

questions.q: When crossing railroad tracks in a manual-transmission vehicle, you should:
options: Stop on the tracks to look both ways
Avoid changing gears while on the tracks
questions.explain: Avoid changing gears on the tracks so you don't stall there.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Trains and vehicles DO NOT MIX: Grade crossing safety tips'

questions.q: Why should you never try to race a train to a crossing?
options: A train is nearer and faster than it appears and may need a mile or more to stop
Trains are slower than they appear
Trains always slow down for cars
questions.explain: A train may need a mile or more to stop, and it is nearer and moving faster than it seems.
questions.ref: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, SOS-133 Rev. 10/2025), Ch. 4, 'Railroad crossings'
